This company makes great products, and they offer excellent customer service too. I have their Fan-tastic Vent fan, the cover (subject of this review) and their Endless Breeze fan, which is a tabletop version (12 volt)of the Fantastic Vent fan.

[[ASIN:B0000AY2Z6 Fan-Tastic Vent 01100WH Endless Breeze 12V Fan]]

Super easy to install. With the right tools, it took me 10-15 min for each cover. YouTube video on installation was a great help ([...]

One slight issue was a cotter pin diameter was ever so slightly larger than the hole of the frame pin. A few passes with a small drill bit opened the hole up enough to get the cotter pin through it. Also, recommend applying a small inner tube patch from a bike tire repair kit between the rubber roof and each frame pin to lessen the wear on the rubber roof.

After installing, we encountered many heavy rain storms. Absolutely no rain water came in...at least not from the vent covers. It was too hot to drive with vents open, so I cannot attest to the cover's effectiveness of keeping the rain out while traveling at 65 mph.

I recently had the the entire roof replaced on my 25' travel trailer. Both vents had MaxAir covers on them - including the original fantastic fan vent in the rear bath. That fan had numerous cracks in the plastic flange and housing (perhaps due to an improper installation of the original vent cover) and had to be replaced. The repair shop doing the roof replacement did not replace the vent cover on the fantastic fan, telling me that "these don't work."

I made plans to add the newer model Max Air fan cover (even though I was hesitant to put a cover designed to mount to metal flange on a plastic flange)... then I found the links to this particular model. While I don't like the fact that mounting required cutting lap sealant, mounting into the roof and re-sealing the screw holes (Remember I just replaced the entire roof due to leaks that couldn't be fixed)... Once this was mounted and in place, I went inside and turned the fan on "high"... and had more air movement in the bath than I've had since this camper was new in 2004! It's perfect - and worth every penny more than the other models would have cost.

This unit performs as advertised, conducts large flow of air very well. My only cons is that the four metal brackets that come with it for installation are not easily adjustable for curved roofs. My RV top is curved and the vent is in the middle. When installing as instructed, the middle of the cover will touch the EPDM membrane in front and in the back. Overtime, this can translate in damage to the EPDM membrane. I wish the brackets didn't have the bolts already mounted on them, so they could be installed upside-down and thus elevate the cover to where it doesn't touch the EPDM rubber.

This vent is not generic adaptable to fantastic fans.  My model is 2000TSC with a temperature control that features a auto "raise" and "lower" to the fan lid.  However the fan lid opens approximately 2" higher then what Vent UB1500 will allow.  Thus the Vent is useless when in a "auto" mode.  To use this vent for the model specified I would have to "manually" set the opening of the fan cover to the Vent cover.  Thus I have a useless application model for my fantastic fan!  Secondly, I went to return the merchandise that cost approximately $57 to the vendor.  UPS wanted over $61 for shipping and USPS wanted $39.  Simple solution to me was to absorb the entire loss and provide a "lowest" rating to this product.  My fantastic fan 2000TSC works great and is a asset to air ventilation on my coach, however it is a pity that our US supplies can not design a Vent cover that would fit generically all fantastic fans.
